output.scope_note: The paper is about polymer solid electrolytes for Li-ion batteries and reports MD-computed ionic conductivities for Li+/TFSI- polymer systems, so it is in scope.

records.measurement_method: MD simulation (LAMMPS, PCFF+) with cluster Nernst-Einstein analysis
records.evidence_quote: The best-performing candidate in the generated set whose p-SMILES code is CC(CNCCOCCOCCOC*)O* achieves a conductivity of 1.13×10-3 S/cm, more than double that of the best polymer in the training set.
records.notes: Polymer-LiTFSI system (1.5 mol/kg salt) from this paper's own MD. Temperature 353 K is from the Methods MD description; the converted 79.85 C is computed from 353 K, not stated in the paper. Conductivity is a candidate value from MD, not an experimental measurement.

records.material_as_written: highest-conductivity polymer in the training set (unnamed; HTP-MD dataset)
records.measurement_method: MD (from prior HTP-MD dataset, cited as refs 32 and 10)
records.evidence_quote: Notably, 17 of the 45 candidates surpass the highest conductivity polymer (conductivity = 5.07×10-4 S/cm) in the training set (Fig. 4c).
records.notes: Value belongs to the previously curated HTP-MD training dataset from the authors' earlier work, so it is treated as literature_cited. The polymer is not named in the text. Figure 4 caption gives the rounded value 5.1×10-4 S/cm; this record uses the text value.
